issue.title: FunctionPreprocessingExpressionVisitor causes early assignment of default type mapping

repository.name: efcore
repository.description: EF Core is a modern object-database mapper for .NET. It supports LINQ queries, change tracking, updates, and schema migrations.

issue.body:
While investigating an issue with case-insensitive StartsWith in Npgsql (https://github.com/npgsql/efcore.pg/issues/388), I ran into some problematic behavior.

In PostgreSQL, case-sensitive strings are represented as a special store type ([citext](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/citext.html)). In order to have proper case-insensitive comparisons, both sides of a comparison expression must be properly typed as citext (`SELECT CAST('HELLO' AS CITEXT) = CAST('hello' AS TEXT)` is false). Now, when the pattern given to StartsWith is a parameter, my string method translator does proper type inference and applies the citext type mapping.

However, FunctionPreprocessingExpressionVisitor detects StartsWith/EndsWith, and introduces a check for whether the pattern is an empty string. Since there is no type inference here, the parameter expression will get whatever the default is for the CLR type (so it's text and not citext). And since this is the first occurrence of the parameter expression encountered by QuerySqlGenerator, the parameter gets configured as a text parameter instead of a citext parameter.

An easy fix for this would be to simply switch the order in the inserted conjunection (i.e. add the empty string check on the right side instead of on the left side). However, I'm wondering why we need this very special casing of StartsWith/EndsWith in a preprocessor rather than handling this logic inside the method translator, as we always do... I can see @maumar introduced this in dbfa82af9b6c0a36c8b30702f16bfd98360ca528 for null semantics, but maybe we can clean/simplify this.

In the meantime I'll work around the issue by adding SQL casts back to citext on the parameter.

issue.title: Query: constant values sometimes get incorrectly parameterized which may lead to issue when the parameter value doesn't match the expected type mapping

repository.name: efcore
repository.description: EF Core is a modern object-database mapper for .NET. It supports LINQ queries, change tracking, updates, and schema migrations.

issue.body:
Found as part of investigation of https://github.com/dotnet/efcore/issues/19128

query:

```cs
context.Set<Gear>()
    .OrderBy(g => g.Nickname)
    .Take(1)
    .Select(g => g.Rank & MilitaryRank.Private))
```

generates the following sql:

```sql
SELECT TOP(@__p_0) [g].[Rank] & @__p_0
FROM [Gears] AS [g]
WHERE [g].[Discriminator] IN (N'Gear', N'Officer')
ORDER BY [g].[Nickname]
```

This happens because we always parameterize arguments to a Skip/Take (value: 1, typed as int).
When processing a projection, we encounter constant enum MilitaryRank.Private, with underlying type also being 1 typed as int. This leads us to substitute the constant with the same parameter.

However the issue is that the expected type mapping for that parameter in the projection is MilitaryRank, not enum. We should not be reusing parameters this way, especially when their type mappings don't match

issue.title: Incorrect query generated when using Skip and Enum Where condition when Skip value is same as enum value

repository.name: efcore
repository.description: EF Core is a modern object-database mapper for .NET. It supports LINQ queries, change tracking, updates, and schema migrations.

issue.body:
<!-- Describe what isn't working as expected -->
Sorry if this problem has been posted before, I couldn't find any issues with similar problem.

Ef core generates invalid SQL when the Skip value is the same as Enum value in a Where condition, when Skip statement is before the Where clause.

I added an example query that generates the expected result (at least considering how it handles the Enum value), but in my current project it is not possible to use that variant (at least not very easily). 
I don't think that it should matter in what order the Skip statement is applied, it shouldn't use the same parameter for the `offset` and `where` predicate. 
Note also that if the Skip value of the original query would be changed to anything else than 0 (the enum value) it would also generate good SQL.

In my current project the issue manifests in the final select projection. Pagination/filters are applied on the inner query and the final query uses a sub query that selects a child entity by applying a similar Enum filter. In Postgresql (database used in the project), because of type mismatch the following error is thrown: `42883: operator does not exist: text = integer` (It tries to compare enum that is stored as `text` with the integer offset parameter).


### Steps to reproduce
Query that generates incorrect SQL
``` C#
 await context.Foos.Skip(0).Where(x => x.Type == FooEnum.A).ToListAsync();
```
Sql generated (notice `@__p_0` parameter usage)
``` SQL
SELECT [t].[Id], [t].[Type]
   FROM (
     SELECT [f].[Id], [f].[Type]
     FROM [Foos] AS [f]
     ORDER BY (SELECT 1)
     OFFSET @__p_0 ROWS
 ) AS [t]
 WHERE [t].[Type] = @__p_0
```

Query that doesn't have the problem (returns expected result). Note Skip was moved after the Where condition
``` C#
 await context.Foos.Where(x => x.Type == FooEnum.A).Skip(0).ToListAsync();
```
Sql generated: 
``` SQL
SELECT [f].[Id], [f].[Type]
FROM [Foos] AS [f]
WHERE [f].[Type] = N'A'
ORDER BY (SELECT 1)
OFFSET 0 ROWS
```
I would expect even the first example to generate the same Where condition: `WHERE [f].[Type] = N'A'`.
Especially because changing the Enum (or Skip) value also generates the expected SQL:
``` C#
 await context.Foos.Skip(0).Where(x => x.Type == FooEnum.B).ToListAsync();
```
Sql generated
``` SQL
SELECT [t].[Id], [t].[Type]
  FROM (
      SELECT [f].[Id], [f].[Type]
      FROM [Foos] AS [f]
      ORDER BY (SELECT 1)
      OFFSET @__p_0 ROWS
  ) AS [t]
  WHERE [t].[Type] = N'B'
```
Or original query with Skip(1):
``` C#
 await context.Foos.Skip(1).Where(x => x.Type == FooEnum.A).ToListAsync();
```
Sql generated
``` SQL
SELECT [t].[Id], [t].[Type]
  FROM (
      SELECT [f].[Id], [f].[Type]
      FROM [Foos] AS [f]
      ORDER BY (SELECT 1)
      OFFSET @__p_0 ROWS
  ) AS [t]
  WHERE [t].[Type] = N'A'
```

Full code example project (has more variations and working examples), uses Sql server local db:
[EfCoreSkipEnumBug.zip](https://github.com/dotnet/efcore/files/5217876/EfCoreSkipEnumBug.zip)



<!--
What steps can we follow to reproduce the issue?

We ❤ code! Include a complete code listing or attach a simplified project

``` C#
Console.WriteLine("Hello, World!");
```

Got Exceptions? Include both the message and the stack trace

For `dotnet ef` and PMC, share the --verbose output
-->



### Further technical details

EF Core version: 3.1.8
Database provider: Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.SqlServer & Npgsql.EntityFrameworkCore.PostgreSQL (maybe also others)
Target framework: .NET Core 3.1
Operating system: Windows 10
IDE: Visual Studio 2019 16.7.2


Thank you.

body:
Proposal: Break `IRelationalParameter` interface and expose TypeMapping.
- Each relational parameter needs to have type mapping assigned to it for us to generate the DbParameter.
- Each relational parameter is different from other if it is taking value of a different client side parameter or it has different typemapping then other relational parameter taking same client side value.

issue.title: Do not generate Convert node in SQL if the converted store type is identical to the operand's

repository.name: efcore
repository.description: EF Core is a modern object-database mapper for .NET. It supports LINQ queries, change tracking, updates, and schema migrations.

issue.body:
There are sometimes scenarios where multiple CLR types can be mapped to the same store type (e.g. PostgreSQL maps Instant, DateTime (with kind UTC), ZonedDateTime (with timezone UTC) and OffsetDateTime (with offset 0) to `timestamp with time zone`; all represent UTC timestamps).

These types contain various conversion methods between one another (e.g. Instant.ToDateTimeUtc returns a UTC DateTime). When translating these, a Convert node is needed to have the correct CLR type, but nothing needs to actually happen in SQL since at the database side it's the same type.

When generating SQL for Convert, we could simply avoid the conversion if the node and the operand node's type mappings' store types are the same.

/cc @smitpatel

issue.title: EF generates invalid SQL when using enums in projections

repository.name: efcore

issue.body:
My team and I stumbled upon a strange behavior while optimizing our internal paging library which is currently blocking us, since we did not find any workaround.

Everytime we project data using a `.Select(...)` and that select contains an enum and its int value matches the value passed in a `.Skip()` or `.Take()` efcore generates invalid sql because it tries to insert the enum ***string*** value into the `SELECT TOP(...)`, `OFFSET ...` or `FETCH NEXT ... ROWS` expression.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/54019893/139068954-ae653896-c9c3-4700-a754-6a26286bba58.png)

I created a repo which reproduces this behavior: https://github.com/mariotebest/efcore_enum_bug

I'm probably missing something very obvious here because I can't imagine an issue like that would stay undetected for several ef core versions (I tried several recent 3.1.x versions on nuget).

issue.title: Query: Add multiple parameters if inferred type mapping differs

repository.name: efcore
repository.description: EF Core is a modern object-database mapper for .NET. It supports LINQ queries, change tracking, updates, and schema migrations.

issue.body:
When adding parameters from query, we check if the type mapping inside TypeMapped parameter is same, if it is not then we add another parameter with different name in SQL.

Clean up in relational parameter builder code
- Remove Dynamic parameter/ property parameter
- Obsolete TypeMappingSource from CommandBuilder
- Remove obsolete code and combine methods which were doing same work

Resolves #19503
Resolves #22524
Resolves #26472
